    A disk has exact area 245π/4245\pi/4245π/4 square centimeters. What is its diameter?

    Answer choices for question 1

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: This is the positive radius; the diameter is twice that length.

    You chose C: This doubles the correct diameter a second time.

    You chose D: This treats 245/4245/4245/4, the radius squared, as the radius and then doubles it.

    Divide the area by pi before taking the positive square root.

    r2=2454,r=752 cm.\begin{aligned} r^2&=\frac{245}{4},\\ r&=\frac{7\sqrt5}{2}\text{ cm}. \end{aligned}r2r​=4245​,=275​​ cm.​

    The diameter contains two radii.

    d=75 cm.d=7\sqrt5\text{ cm}.d=75​ cm.
  2. 2

    A selected arc is five fourths as long as the circle's positive radius. What is its central turn in radians?

    Answer choices for question 2

    Solution

    Correct answer: D

    You chose A: This reverses the defining quotient and divides radius by arc length.

    You chose B: This inserts pi into a radian measure even though the given arc-to-radius ratio is 5/45/45/4.

    You chose C: This divides the selected arc by the diameter instead of the radius.

    Radian measure compares the selected curved length with the radius in the same unit.

    θ=sr.\theta=\frac{s}{r}.θ=rs​.

    The given ratio therefore makes the turn 5/45/45/4 radians. Radian measures need not contain pi.

    An annulus has outer radius 17/217/217/2 cm and inner radius 5/25/25/2 cm. What is the total length of its complete boundary?

    Answer choices for question 3

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    You chose B: This subtracts the two circumferences instead of adding the two boundary circles.

    You chose C: This counts only the outer circle and omits the hole boundary.

    You chose D: This is the annulus area coefficient times pi, obtained by subtracting squared radii, rather than its boundary length.

    The material touches both circular edges, so both circumferences contribute.

    P=2π(172+52),P=22π cm.\begin{aligned} P&=2\pi\left(\frac{17}{2}+\frac52\right),\\ P&=22\pi\text{ cm}. \end{aligned}PP​=2π(217​+25​),=22π cm.​

    A circle has diameter 313131 cm, with endpoints A,CA,CA,C. Two equal helper circles centered at A,CA,CA,C must cross at two distinct points. Which common compass opening permits this?

    Answer choices for question 4

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: The two helper radii total only 242424 cm, less than the 313131 cm center separation, so the circles are disjoint.

    You chose B: The two helper radii total 303030 cm, still less than the 313131 cm center separation.

    You chose D: This is exactly half the center separation, so the helper circles merely touch at the original center.

    For two equal circles with distinct centers, two crossings require the common opening to exceed half the center separation.

    k>312 cm.k>\frac{31}{2}\text{ cm}.k>231​ cm.

    Only the 181818 cm opening exceeds 15.515.515.5 cm. Equality gives just one contact point, which cannot determine a perpendicular-bisector line.

  5. 5

    One circle has diameter 181818 cm and another has diameter 272727 cm. Which argument justifies equal circumference-to-diameter ratios without measuring their curved boundaries?

    Answer choices for question 5

    Solution

    Correct answer: C

    You chose A: This applies the squared area scale factor to a length. Circumference scales by 3/23/23/2, so this argument would change the ratio.

    You chose B: Similarity preserves shape, but a nonunit dilation changes circumference. Equal circumferences with different diameters would give unequal ratios.

    You chose D: The second diameter is 272727 cm, so it also grows by 3/23/23/2. Holding it fixed prevents the needed cancellation.

    A positive dilation maps the first circle to the second. Every straight side in an inner or outer polygon scales by 3/23/23/2. Because those polygons can enclose the curved length as tightly as needed, the circumference has that same length factor.

    (3/2)C(3/2)d=Cd.\frac{(3/2)C}{(3/2)d}=\frac{C}{d}.(3/2)d(3/2)C​=dC​.

    The factor cancels for every positive dilation. Thus every positive-radius circle has the same dimensionless ratio, pi.

    A regular hexagon is constructed by radius-length compass steps. A second hexagon is constructed with the same opening in the same circle, starting at the midpoint of one minor arc between consecutive vertices of the first. How many vertices do the two hexagons share?

    Answer choices for question 14

    Solution

    Correct answer: B

    You chose A: This assumes that the radius fixes the starting point as well as the step size. The second construction starts halfway between first-hexagon vertices.

    You chose C: This assumes that the first hexagon's diameter endpoints remain vertices after a 30-degree shift. Each of those endpoints shifts too.

    You chose D: This confuses selecting alternate vertices of one hexagon with shifting all six vertices halfway to their neighbors.

    Each radius-length chord gives a 60∘60^\circ60∘ central step. The new starting radius is halfway through one such step, a 30∘30^\circ30∘ offset.

    60∘2=30∘.\frac{60^\circ}{2}=30^\circ.260∘​=30∘.

    Every later new vertex retains that offset: equal 60∘60^\circ60∘ advances put each halfway between consecutive old vertices. A 30∘30^\circ30∘ offset cannot equal a whole number of 60∘60^\circ60∘ steps, so no vertices coincide.

    A given circle has center OOO, radius r>0r>0r>0 and diameter endpoints A,CA,CA,C. Equal helper circles centered at A,CA,CA,C use a common positive opening kkk. Exactly which range of kkk makes them cross at two distinct points that both lie strictly inside the given circle?

    Solution

    Correct answer: A

    Every pair of distinct helper crossings lies on the perpendicular bisector of ACACAC. Let ttt be either crossing's positive distance from OOO. A right triangle has hypotenuse kkk and one leg rrr.

    Two distinct crossings strictly inside the original circle require 0<t<r0<t<r0<t<r. Squaring positive lengths and substituting gives

    A circle has radius 121212 cm and circumference CCC cm. Its regular inscribed polygons have perimeter P<80P<80P<80 cm and apothem hhh. The parallel tangent polygons have perimeter QQQ.

    For every positive numerical tolerance ε\varepsilonε, a refinement can achieve both gaps, measured in centimeters:

    Q−P<ε,12−h<ε.\begin{aligned} Q-P&<\varepsilon,\\ 12-h&<\varepsilon. \end{aligned}Q−P12−h​<ε,<ε.​

    Define the polygon areas and a proposed disk-area value, in square centimeters:

    U−I<46ε.U-I<46\varepsilon.U−I<46ε.

    For any proposed positive area difference, choose epsilon smaller than that difference divided by 464646. Both A,TA,TA,T remain inside a narrower common enclosure, ruling out that difference. Therefore

    A=T.A=T.A=T.

Problem 1 of 10

  1. Problem 1 Two circular sizes

    A circle has exact diameter 23/423/423/4 cm. A second circle is its dilation by the positive factor 8/58/58/5.

    (a) Find the first circle's circumference and disk area exactly.

    (b) Find the second circle's circumference and disk area exactly.

    Text description of this figure

    The diameter crosses center O and is 23/4 centimeters long. No recovered length or area is shown.

    1. Hint 1

      Circumference is a length, while disk area responds to a scale factor in two dimensions.

    2. Hint 2

      Halve the first diameter before finding area. The second circumference has factor 8/58/58/5 and the second area has factor (8/5)2(8/5)^2(8/5)2.

    Answer

    (a)

    C1=23π4 cmA1=529π64 cm2\begin{gathered}C_1=\frac{23\pi}{4}\text{ cm}\\A_1=\frac{529\pi}{64}\text{ cm}^2\end{gathered}C1​=423π​ cmA1​=64529π​ cm2​

    (b)

    C2=46π5 cmA2=529π25 cm2\begin{gathered}C_2=\frac{46\pi}{5}\text{ cm}\\A_2=\frac{529\pi}{25}\text{ cm}^2\end{gathered}C2​=546π​ cmA2​=25529π​ cm2​

    Full solution

    (a) A diameter gives circumference directly.

    C1=23π4 cm.C_1=\frac{23\pi}{4}\text{ cm}.C1​=423π​ cm.

    The positive radius is half that diameter.

    r1=238 cm.r_1=\frac{23}{8}\text{ cm}.r1​=823​ cm.

    Square it for disk area.

    A1=529π64 cm2.A_1=\frac{529\pi}{64}\text{ cm}^2.A1​=64529π​ cm2.

    (b) A dilation scales circumference by its length factor.

      Use the two endpoints of one diameter as centers of equal helper circles. An opening equal to the whole diameter gives two distinct crossings.

    3. Hint 3

      Join the helper crossings, then use its intersections with the original circle. A right center triangle supplies the side, and its perpendicular half gives the apothem.

    Helpers at A,CA,CA,C use opening 979\sqrt797​ cm. Lengths in cm:

    s=9142a=9144P=1814\begin{gathered}s=\frac{9\sqrt{14}}2\\a=\frac{9\sqrt{14}}4\\P=18\sqrt{14}\end{gathered}s=2914​​a=4914​​P=1814​​

    Draw a diameter ACACAC through OOO.

    Mark its original-circle intersections B,DB,DB,D.

  6. Problem 6 Recover the sector

    A proper sector has area 54 cm254\text{ cm}^254 cm2 and complete perimeter 363636 cm. Its positive radius and selected central turn are unknown. The turn must be strictly between zero and 2π2\pi2π radians.

    The complete perimeter includes both radii.

    s=36−2r.s=36-2r.s=36−2r.

    The area is half radius times selected arc length.

    54=12r(36−2r)r2−18r+54=0(r−9)2=27.\begin{aligned}54&=\frac12r(36-2r)\\r^2-18r+54&=0\\(r-9)^2&=27.\end{aligned}54r2−18r+54(r−9)2​=21​r(36−2r)=0=27.​

    Both algebraic radii are positive.

    Their corresponding arc lengths come from the same boundary equation.

    For the larger radius, the selected length and radian turn are

    For the smaller radius, the arc length is 18+6318+6\sqrt318+63​ cm and the turn is 4+234+2\sqrt34+23​ radians.

    The finite hexagon enclosure gives pi less than 232\sqrt323​.

    This turn exceeds a full turn and cannot bound the stated proper sector.

    The retained radius and arc give perimeter 363636 cm.

    Their product is 108 cm2108\text{ cm}^2108 cm2, so half that product is the stated area 54 cm254\text{ cm}^254 cm2.

    There is exactly one admissible sector.

  7. Problem 7 Marks that close around a circle

    A circle has known center OOO, radius 37\sqrt{37}37​ cm and boundary point AAA. Copy it on paper at any convenient scale.

    (a) Construct regular hexagon ABCDEFABCDEFABCDEF with a compass and unmarked straightedge, keeping every compass arc. Name the center, opening and excluded intersection at every forward step, including the return to AAA. Justify closure and regularity.

    (b) Construct an equilateral triangle from alternate hexagon vertices and justify its equal sides. Find the exact hexagon apothem and area, and the exact triangle area.

    Text description of this figure

    Only the given circle, center O, point A and radius OA of square root 37 centimeters are drawn. No other vertices or construction arcs are present.

    1. Hint 1

      The compass can carry the given radius around the original circle as a straight chord length.

    2. Hint 2

      At each new vertex, discard the crossing that would return to the preceding vertex. Equal-radius center triangles determine how much each forward step turns.

    3. Hint 3

      Join alternate justified vertices. Bisect one hexagon center triangle to obtain the perpendicular apothem, then use the polygon perimeter-apothem area relationship.

    Answer

    Construct hexagon ABCDEFABCDEFABCDEF with opening OAOAOA and triangle ACEACEACE.

    aH=1112 cmAH=11132 cm2AT=11134 cm2\begin{gathered}a_H=\frac{\sqrt{111}}2\text{ cm}\\A_H=\frac{111\sqrt3}{2}\text{ cm}^2\\A_T=\frac{111\sqrt3}{4}\text{ cm}^2\end{gathered}aH​=2111​​ cmAH​=21113​​ cm2AT​=41113​​ cm2​

    Full solution

    (a) Set the opening to OAOAOA.

    With center AAA, choose one of its two crossings with the original circle as BBB.

    This fixes a travel direction.

    Keep the opening unchanged for every later arc.

    Center B: mark C at the original-circle crossing other than A.

    Center C: mark D at the original-circle crossing other than B.

    Center D: mark E at the original-circle crossing other than C.

    Center E: mark F at the original-circle crossing other than D.

    Center F: the crossing other than E returns to A.

    Retain the arcs from all six centers and join A, B, C, D, E, F, A in order.

    Every step's chord equals the compass opening.

    Its two radii belong to the original circle and have that same length.

    Each center triangle is equilateral, so each forward turn is 60∘60^\circ60∘.

    Six turns make 360∘360^\circ360∘; the first five are smaller than a full turn and locate distinct vertices.

    Adjacent center triangles give equal 120-degree interior angles.

    Thus the closed polygon has equal sides and equal angles.

    (b) Join ACACAC, CECECE and EAEAEA.

    Each spans two consecutive 60-degree center turns.

    The three center triangles have equal radii and equal included 120-degree angles, so SAS gives three equal chords.

    Triangle ACEACEACE is equilateral.

    The hexagon side is 37\sqrt{37}37​ cm.

    Its right half-center triangle has hypotenuse 37\sqrt{37}37​ cm and half-side 37/2\sqrt{37}/237​/2 cm.

    Its perpendicular apothem is therefore

    aH=1112 cm.a_H=\frac{\sqrt{111}}2\text{ cm}.aH​=2111​​ cm.

    The perimeter is 6376\sqrt{37}637​ cm.

    The apothem provides the height in the area sum.

    The triangle side is 111\sqrt{111}111​ cm and its apothem is 37/2\sqrt{37}/237​/2 cm, from the right halves of a 120-degree center triangle.

    Use its own perimeter and apothem.

    AT=12(3111)372AT=11134 cm2.\begin{aligned}A_T&=\frac12(3\sqrt{111})\frac{\sqrt{37}}2\\A_T&=\frac{111\sqrt3}{4}\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}AT​AT​​=21​(3111​)237​​=41113​​ cm2.​

    Answer

    Construct hexagon ABCDEFABCDEFABCDEF with opening OAOAOA and triangle ACEACEACE.

    aH=1112 cmAH=11132 cm2AT=11134 cm2\begin{gathered}a_H=\frac{\sqrt{111}}2\text{ cm}\\A_H=\frac{111\sqrt3}{2}\text{ cm}^2\\A_T=\frac{111\sqrt3}{4}\text{ cm}^2\end{gathered}aH​=2111​​ cmAH​=21113​​ cm2AT​=41113​​ cm2​

    Key idea

    Retained radius-opening arcs prove the hexagon, and alternate vertices transfer that justification to an equilateral triangle.

  9. Problem 9 How tight can the enclosure become?

After nnn refinements, where nnn is a positive integer, let the new side length be sss, inner perimeter PPP, inner apothem hhh and parallel tangent-polygon perimeter QQQ, all in centimeters.

    P<50h>2.\begin{gathered}P<50\\h>2.\end{gathered}P<50h>2.​

    Each arc bisection makes the squared side length less than half its preceding value.

    (a) Express 7−h7-h7−h in terms of s,hs,hs,h from a right half-center triangle. Obtain a bound for Q−PQ-PQ−P in terms of nnn, and find the fewest refinements for which your bound certifies a perimeter gap less than 0.010.010.01 cm.

    (b) Derive the exact disk area in terms of CCC from the polygon enclosures. Explain why a positive discrepancy is impossible, and state the corresponding formula for any positive radius rrr.

    (c) Does rearranging this disk into a row of 646464 equal curved sectors make an exact parallelogram? Explain the finite figure's role.

    1. Hint 1

      The half-side and apothem are perpendicular legs, while the circle radius is their hypotenuse.

    2. Hint 2

      Factor the difference of the squared radius and squared apothem. Then use the given side-shrinking rate.

    3. Hint 3

      The parallel tangent polygon has perimeter Q=7P/hQ=7P/hQ=7P/h. The bounds on P,hP,hP,h control the factor multiplying the radial gap.

    4. Hint 4

      For area, compare the two polygon areas and the value they approach. A nonzero fixed difference cannot fit inside every sufficiently narrow enclosure.

    Answer

    (a) 7−h=s2/[4(7+h)]7-h=s^2/[4(7+h)]7−h=s2/[4(7+h)]. Gap less than 175/(4⋅2n)175/(4\cdot2^n)175/(4⋅2n) cm; 131313 refinements suffice by this bound. (b)

    A=7C/2.A=7C/2.A=7C/2.

    In general A=Cr/2A=Cr/2A=Cr/2. (c) No; a finite row retains curved edges.

    Full solution

    (a) The right half-center triangle gives

    49=h2+s24.49=h^2+\frac{s^2}{4}.49=h2+4s2​.

    Factor the difference of squares and divide by the positive sum.

    7−h=s24(7+h).7-h=\frac{s^2}{4(7+h)}.7−h=4(7+h)s2​.

    Since h>0h>0h>0, this is less than s2/28s^2/28s2/28.

    The original hexagon side is 777 cm.

    After nnn positive refinements the squared side satisfies

    s2<492n.s^2<\frac{49}{2^n}.s2<2n49​.

    The tangent polygon is the 7/h7/h7/h dilation of the inner polygon.

    Its perimeter difference is

    Q−P=P(7−h)h.Q-P=\frac{P(7-h)}h.Q−P=hP(7−h)​.

    Use P<50P<50P<50, h>2h>2h>2 and the radial-gap bound.

    Q−P<25s228Q−P<1754⋅2n cm.\begin{aligned}Q-P&<\frac{25s^2}{28}\\Q-P&<\frac{175}{4\cdot2^n}\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}Q−PQ−P​<2825s2​<4⋅2n175​ cm.​

    For this bound to certify the requested accuracy, its denominator must satisfy

    2n>4375.2^n>4375.2n>4375.

    Twelve refinements give 409640964096, which is too small for this bound.

    Thirteen give 819281928192, so thirteen is the fewest refinements this bound certifies.

    This is not a claim that the actual gap first crosses the threshold at that stage.

    (b) Let III and UUU be the inner and outer polygon areas.

    Their perpendicular heights give

    I=Ph/2U=7Q/2.\begin{gathered}I=Ph/2\\U=7Q/2.\end{gathered}I=Ph/2U=7Q/2.​

    The disk area lies between them.

    So does 7C/27C/27C/2, because the circumference lies between the two perimeters and h<7h<7h<7.

    Both the perimeter gap and radial gap become smaller than any chosen positive tolerance.

    Their area contributions are

    U−I=72(Q−P)+P2(7−h).U-I=\frac72(Q-P)+\frac P2(7-h).U−I=27​(Q−P)+2P​(7−h).

    The perimeter P stays bounded, so the area gap also becomes as small as requested.

    If the disk area and 7C/27C/27C/2 differed by a fixed positive amount, a narrower common enclosure would be impossible.

    Therefore

    A=7C/2.A=7C/2.A=7C/2.

    Nothing in that reasoning depends on radius 7.

    For any positive radius the same argument gives

    A=Cr/2.A=Cr/2.A=Cr/2.

    Substituting the circumference expression gives A=πr2.A=\pi r^2.A=πr2.

    (c) Rigidly rearranging the 646464 sectors preserves their total area exactly.

    Their circular edges remain curved, so this finite row is not a parallelogram.

    Finer rearrangements support the limiting comparison; an exact area conclusion needs control of the remaining discrepancy, as in the polygon enclosure argument.

    Answer

    (a) 7−h=s2/[4(7+h)]7-h=s^2/[4(7+h)]7−h=s2/[4(7+h)]. Gap less than 175/(4⋅2n)175/(4\cdot2^n)175/(4⋅2n) cm; 131313 refinements suffice by this bound. (b)

    A=7C/2.A=7C/2.A=7C/2.

    In general A=Cr/2A=Cr/2A=Cr/2. (c) No; a finite row retains curved edges.

    Key idea

    Exhaustion establishes equality by ruling out every positive discrepancy, while each finite approximation still has an error.

    ▾

  10. Problem 10 One side becomes a cut

    An equilateral triangle ABCABCABC is inscribed in a circle centered at OOO. Its perimeter is 9219\sqrt{21}921​ cm.

    Remove the minor circular segment between side ABABAB and the minor arc with those endpoints. Keep the rest of the disk.

    Find the exact kept area and complete perimeter. Explain which perpendicular triangle height your area calculation needs, and why the full altitude from CCC is a different length.

    Text description of this figure

    Equilateral triangle ABC is inscribed in circle O. The minor cap on side AB is removed. The major segment containing C is shaded, with chord AB and the major arc as its solid boundary. The triangle perimeter is nine square root twenty-one centimeters.

    1. Hint 1

      The triangle perimeter determines its side, which in turn determines the supporting circle radius.

    2. Hint 2

      Bisect the 120-degree center triangle on the cut side. Its perpendicular center-to-side distance is the apothem.

    3. Hint 3

      The kept region is the complement of the minor cap. Its complete boundary has the same chord and the longer arc through the third triangle vertex.

    Answer

    A=(42π+6334) cm2P=(4π7+321) cm\begin{gathered}A=\left(42\pi+\frac{63\sqrt3}{4}\right)\text{ cm}^2\\P=(4\pi\sqrt7+3\sqrt{21})\text{ cm}\end{gathered}A=(42π+4633​​) cm2P=(4π7​+321​) cm​

    The needed center-triangle height is 37/23\sqrt7/237​/2 cm; the full altitude is 97/29\sqrt7/297​/2 cm.

    Full solution

    The triangle side is one third of its perimeter, or 3213\sqrt{21}321​ cm.

    An inscribed equilateral triangle side is square root 3 times its circle radius.

    Thus

    r=37 cm.r=3\sqrt7\text{ cm}.r=37​ cm.

    Side ABABAB subtends one of three equal 120-degree center angles.

    The right halves of triangle OABOABOAB have hypotenuse r and shorter leg equal to half r.

    The perpendicular center-to-side height is therefore

    OM=372 cm.OM=\frac{3\sqrt7}{2}\text{ cm}.OM=237​​ cm.

    This is the apothem.

    The full altitude from C contains the radius from C to O as well, giving 97/29\sqrt7/297​/2 cm.

    The minor sector is one third of the disk.

    The central triangle uses side AB as base and OM as height.

    Asector=21π cm2AOAB=6334 cm2.\begin{gathered}A_{\rm sector}=21\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{OAB}=\frac{63\sqrt3}{4}\text{ cm}^2.\end{gathered}Asector​=21π cm2AOAB​=4633​​ cm2.​

    Using the full altitude would instead find the area of the entire equilateral triangle ABC.

    Subtract the central triangle from the minor sector to get the removed cap.

    Then subtract that cap from the whole disk.

    Acap=21π−6334Akept=63π−AcapAkept=42π+6334.\begin{aligned}A_{\text{cap}}&=21\pi-\frac{63\sqrt3}{4}\\A_{\rm kept}&=63\pi-A_{\text{cap}}\\A_{\rm kept}&=42\pi+\frac{63\sqrt3}{4}.\end{aligned}Acap​Akept​Akept​​=21π−4633​​=63π−Acap​=42π+4633​​.​

    These areas are in square centimeters.

    The kept major arc uses two thirds of the circumference.

    smajor=4π7 cm.s_{\rm major}=4\pi\sqrt7\text{ cm}.smajor​=4π7​ cm.

    Its straight boundary is the chord AB, of length 3213\sqrt{21}321​ cm.

    Hence

    P=(4π7+321) cm.P=(4\pi\sqrt7+3\sqrt{21})\text{ cm}.P=(4π7​+321​) cm.

    The other two triangle sides are interior guides and add no exposed boundary.

    Answer

    A=(42π+6334) cm2P=(4π7+321) cm\begin{gathered}A=\left(42\pi+\frac{63\sqrt3}{4}\right)\text{ cm}^2\\P=(4\pi\sqrt7+3\sqrt{21})\text{ cm}\end{gathered}A=(42π+4633​​) cm2P=(4π7​+321​) cm​

    The needed center-triangle height is 37/23\sqrt7/237​/2 cm; the full altitude is 97/29\sqrt7/297​/2 cm.

    Key idea

    Transfer through the supporting radius, then use the selected segment and the correct perpendicular height.
